title: How do you generate high quality 3D game assets?
author: Separate_Importance2
selftext:
I’m fairly new to game development and I’ve been messing around with Astra to build a shooter. The results I’ve been getting are fairly rough with blocky assets and environment. I’ve tried asking it to look online for free game assets to use but it seems unwilling to use a lot of them citing licensing issues (even unwilling CC licensed assets). It seems like getting and generating assets is the bottleneck to AI dev, or am I doing something wrong here?  
Can anyone share a good workflow to generate a fairly realistic 3D game?

comments.author: HowzitGarrn
comments.body: Tripo smart mesh P2 model. First use AI image gen to come up with the concept art, then tell the image generator to extract things one by one from the concept art. After that, get Tripo to model each piece separately, then you assemble it together in Blender.

replies.author: Separate_Importance2
replies.body: What’s the difference between using Tripo and just let gpt use blender to create the asset directly?

comments.author: Murph4321
comments.body: Honestly I was the same and didn't want any subscriptions and was only looking for free things. But I ended up getting tripo and it was the best decision progress wise for making assets. Generate a concept image in gpt. Tweak it till your happy with it. Then put it into tripo and generally get a good quality 3d asset

comments.author: Kindly-Sail6260
comments.body: Hunyuan tencent. You can generate quality assets there. They’re not perfect but they also have a retopology section you can use to have usable models. Just don’t think they’ll look too nice

replies.author: Separate_Importance2
replies.body: I’ll give that a shot a well thanks

replies.author: XalAtoh
replies.body: Nah, random SAAS era is over, just use ChatGpt/Claude.

comments.author: No-Association-1834
comments.body: If I am not looking for very Specific one , i download CC0 , CCBY or Free Standard ones from Sketchfab or CGTraders.

comments.author: Salt-Willingness-513
comments.body: Chatgpt imagegen -> meshy 2k multi view asset, rigging -> claude/codex asset cleanup

replies.author: TheBigQuestion354
replies.body: I’ve been making models recently and what’s really cool is I have miniatures that I can picture, send through Astra for refinement (AI image generation), then send through Tripo. Works really well!

comments.author: BoringCanary
comments.body: ChatGPT for render images, then Tripo/Meshy > blender /unreal

replies.author: Separate_Importance2
replies.body: Does tripo output a file that I can put directly into unreal or do I need to send it to blender first?

replies.author: HurryOne
replies.body: You have to put it into blender first.

replies.author: Separate_Importance2
replies.body: Got it. Thanks. I’m playing around with Tripo, it seems like the ChatGPT plugin is an api with separate billing from the website studio version. How do you guys deal with that? Do you just manually use the website to generate the asset?

comments.author: EchoingAngel
comments.body: Rodin is the best tool for high quality, medium count triangles. Meshy and Tripo really struggle to get things down to acceptable triangle counts

comments.author: PrintableNapalm
comments.body: They are all bad tbh. They look okay in a compressed video on your phone, but they don't normally hold up on close inspection.

comments.author: Nilo_Team
comments.body:
yeah asset gen is the bottleneck with agents-

nilo.io is free in the browser (monthly bits)- gen the props / env / chars there, hit model settings + LOD to cut the blocky poly mess, export GLB/FBX into unreal (or whatever). no blender required for the mesh itself- auto-rig only bipedal T-pose tho. LMK if you try it :)

replies.author: Nilo_Team
replies.body: (you can pick which 3D model provider to use in Nilo, too....)

comments.author: 5StarAlpha
comments.body:
My son tried a few paid ones briefly and settled on Meshy.  
We usually do 4k to have the high res and it’s about 2-3m vertices. Then remesh to something like 30k.

Rigging was okay for a human but still lot of adjustments in blender and weight adjustments. Could nit get the quadruped rigging to work. Then we discovered we could just ask open ai to do rigging and even create animations.

This is a school project and he is taking some online gaming design courses, Unreal tutorials and is supposed to document the process.

If you are curious, here is his blog post about the 3d render process.

https://phantomwoods.com/my-journey-part-2-turning-squirrel-pictures-into-3d-models/

Not selling anything. It’s just to learn about using AI for game dev for school and hopefully a project to help him with college applications this fall.

replies.author: Separate_Importance2
replies.body: This is a great breakdown, I appreciate you sharing it, definitely helped a lot
